page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by the Nitro hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R32 processor operating at 3.3 GHz, it provides 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with multithreading support. Memory capacity measures 192 GB of DDR4 clocked at 3 GHz, offering a 1:2 compute-to-memory distribution of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled directly via 3,800 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, accompanied by a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no discrete graphics accelerators.

Performance benchmarks show substantial capabilities in multi-threaded computation alongside modest single-core throughput. Synthetic single-core evaluations place the instance in the lower tier for stress-ng and average for Geekbench at 1314.0. Conversely, parallel metrics demonstrate strong execution, scoring 44224.0 in Clang software compilation and 71423.0 in ray tracing. In PassMark testing, the platform reaches a strong overall CPU score of 67778.59 and top-tier encryption throughput at 98126.63. Memory subsystems support 80.73 million Redis SET operations per second, aided by high cached bandwidth.

The combination of high core counts and 3,800 GB of direct NVMe storage provides strong resource density for data-heavy and parallel jobs. Workloads requiring sustained multi-core efficiency, such as distributed compilation pipelines, batch transformations, in-memory caching, and local database operations, map directly to its strengths, though applications constrained primarily by single-thread execution latency may experience bottlenecks.
description: Amazon Web Services c5ad.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server driven by a 48-core, 96-thread AMD EPYC 7R32 processor at 3.3 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance pairs 192 GB of DDR4 memory across an x86_64 architecture with 3,800 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. System benchmarks highlight superior multi-threaded compute and cryptographic processing, reinforced by top-tier PassMark encryption marks and strong results in Clang compilation, ray tracing, and database operations. Memory-centric evaluations confirm robust caching performance alongside 80.73 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-core performance tests yield lower relative metrics, the substantial core density and fast local disk array establish c5ad.24xlarge as an efficient host for parallel batch workloads, software build automation, high-throughput caching, and data processing pipelines.
